title: The promise of molecular gates and what comes next
summary: Gate Bioscience is developing a new class of medicines designed to eliminate disease-causing proteins at their source. In this episode of "The Top Line," Gate co-founder and CEO Jordi Mata-Fink, Ph.D., discusses the promise of molecular gates, the biotech's expanded partnership with Eli Lilly and its plans to bring the technology into the clinic.

title: Rezolute gets an uplift from phase 3 tumor hyperinsulinism win ahead of FDA meeting
summary: A phase 3 clinical trial of Rezolute’s ersodetug in tumor hyperinsulinism has hit its primary endpoint, boosting the biotech ahead of a potential filing for FDA approval in another indication.

title: Cellectis will shed 70% of workforce as part of in vivo pivot
summary: Cellectis’ pivot from allogeneic CAR-Ts to in vivo therapies is set to come at the expense of 70% of its workforce.

title: ‘They’ve been misdiagnosed for too long’: Researchers use 10-protein panel to improve ALS detection
summary: By the time a neurodegenerative condition has been diagnosed, it's often too late. At the point of detection, the disease may already be causing irreversible damage, fueling an urgent search for ways to identify biological clues earlier and track their progression.

title: Chutes & Ladders—Bristol Myers' research chief out amid R&D reorganization
summary: Bristol Myers Squibb's research chief is departing as the company restructures R&D. Summit Therapeutics cut ties with multiple launch team members, including its CCO, ahead of a high-stakes FDA decision. And OncoNano appointed its interim chief, a former FDA commissioner, to the permanent CEO spot.

title: American Cancer Society updates prostate cancer screening guidance
summary: For the first time in 16 years, the American Cancer Society (ACS) has updated its guideline for prostate cancer screening as it drives to boost detection of the disease before it spreads.

title: Sanofi-backed Windward hits $225M IPO goal, as Rezera delays listing over ‘market conditions’
summary: Windward Bio’s IPO has blown to exactly the spot the Swiss biotech had been aiming for, bringing in $225 million to fund a pair of respiratory drugs licensed from China.

title: Virtuoso Surgical nabs FDA authorization for robotic bladder lesions system
summary: The FDA has granted De Novo authorization for Virtuoso Surgical’s Virtuoso Endoscopy System.

title: Regeneron posts positive phase 2 data for baloncibart in nervous system disorder, eyes pivotal trial
summary: Regeneron has posted positive phase 2 data on baloncibart in postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome, teeing the biotech up to start a potentially pivotal trial in the first half of 2027.

title: ARPA-H bets $4.9 million on ibogaine for PTSD treatment in veterans
summary: The U.S. department of health and human services announced a $4.9 million bet to advance the development of ibogaine for post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD).

title: FDA appears to pause controversial speedy review program, complete response letter disclosures
summary: The FDA has quietly shelved the Commissioner’s National Priority Voucher (CNPV) pilot program, Reuters reports. Meanwhile, the agency also appears to have paused publishing complete response letters after briefly halting—and then resuming—the practice in July.

title: Vor pays RemeGen $10M for long-acting addition to autoimmune pipeline
summary: Vor Bio is paying RemeGen $10 million upfront in cash for rights to RC298 outside Greater China, adding a long-acting drug candidate to its BAFF/APRIL franchise.

title: Kyverna abandons next-gen autoimmune CAR-T once touted as follow-up to miv-cel
summary: Kyverna is halting work on a next-gen CD19 CAR-T therapy as the biotech seeks FDA approval for what could become the first CAR-T treatment for an autoimmune disease.

title: Why a fresh approach to targeting G protein-coupled receptors could treat a rare eye cancer
summary: Researchers found that only by targeting both the G protein-coupled receptor and its mutated internal molecular switch can uveal melanoma cell signaling be disrupted.

title: BMS reunites R&D divisions under Cristian Massacesi, while Robert Plenge departs
summary: Bristol Myers Squibb is merging its research and development divisions under the leadership of Cristian Massacesi, M.D.

title: Pfizer taps Blackstone for up to $1.5B to pave path to GLP-1's obesity launch
summary: Pfizer has secured up to $1.5 billion from Blackstone Life Sciences to fund development of its monthly GLP-1 receptor agonist.

title: Addex spinout Neurosterix raises $105M series B to fund phase 2 schizophrenia trial
summary: Addex Therapeutics’ neuropsychiatric-focused spinout has raised $105 million in series B funds to bankroll a planned phase 2 study of its schizophrenia treatment.

title: Valo and Montai become one as the Flagship AI-based biotechs tie the knot
summary: Two Flagship Pioneering-founded AI drug discovery and development biotechs, Valo Health and Montai Therapeutics, will join forces in a merger that aims to advance Montai’s early-stage and preclinical pipeline as well as continue a series of big-name partnerships already in tow.

title: Rivia launches AI-powered clinical trial data review module, with Scancell as early adopter
summary: Swiss data engine Rivia has launched a new AI-powered data review module to speed up clinical data cleaning.

title: BioNTech pays $205M for FDA voucher to speed up ‘late-stage oncology pipeline’
summary: BioNTech has agreed to pay $205 million to purchase an FDA priority review voucher to support a future filing of a drug in its “late-stage oncology pipeline.” Fierce breaks down which candidate is most likely to claim the regulatory accelerator.

title: Amgen builds Sjögren’s case with detailed phase 3 data ahead of Novartis showdown
summary: Amgen has shared more data from a phase 3 Sjögren’s disease trial that dazzled analysts, digging into the details that could shape its showdown with Novartis.

title: Enhancer-targeted CRISPR-A rescues haploinsufficiency and mutant phenotypes in organoid models of autism
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 13 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02504-9CRISPR activation targeted to enhancers of autism risk genes CHD8 and SCN2A selectively increased expression and reversed mutant phenotypes in both patient-derived and gene-edited neuron and cortical organoid models of autism.

title: Gene discovery and pleiotropic architecture of multidimensional pain in a genome-wide association study of >1.2 million individuals
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 12 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02455-1We conducted a meta-analytic genome-wide association study of multidimensional pain in >1.2 million European-ancestry individuals. We identified 343 independent loci, which, alongside findings from a sex-stratified GWAS and other analyses, expand our knowledge of the genetics of pain.

title: Information formatting in neuronal populations predicts differential functional contributions to behavior
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 10 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02514-7Using experiments in monkeys and modeling, the authors demonstrate that the formatting of population information predicts the contribution of different brain areas to behavior.

title: Why Viruses Make You Sneeze: COVID Proteins Directly Hijack Sensory Nerves
summary: Why do colds, flu, and COVID make us sneeze, cough, and ache? Researchers found the SARS-CoV-2 enzymes directly hijack pain-sensing airway nerves via the "wasabi receptor" (TRPA1), triggering symptoms independently of immune inflammation.
category: Featured, Neuroscience, brain research, COVID-19, neurobiology, sensory neuroscience, UC Berkeley

title: Genetic Switch Helped Evolve the Large Primate Brain
summary: How did the human brain evolve to be so large and complex? Researchers discovered a primate-specific DNA regulatory switch controlling the shared DACH1 gene, boosting specialized basal radial glia stem cells that build the cerebral cortex without needing new genes.
category: Events, Genetics, Neuroscience, brain evolution, brain research, evolution, evolutionary neuroscience, neurobiology

title: CRISPR Enhancer Editing Rescues Autism Brain Organoids
summary: Rather than cutting DNA, scientists used precision CRISPR activation aimed at natural gene "dials" to boost healthy copies of CHD8 and SCN2A in human brain organoids, restoring normal tissue growth and neuronal firing exclusively in mutated cells.
category: Autism, Featured, Genetics, Neuroscience, ASD, brain development, brain research, developmental neuroscience, neurobiology, neurodevelopment, UCLA

title: Mapping the Brain’s Energy Budget: How ATP Fuels Thought
summary: How much energy does a single thought cost? The study will map the brain's metabolic budget across scales, solving why active neurons burn sugar rapidly and how brain cells survive oxygen loss.
category: Featured, Neuroscience, ATP, Boston University, brain research, cognition, neurobiology

title: Hidden Body Map in Brain Explains Complex Coordination
summary: How do you effortlessly coordinate your hand, arm, head, and lips to sip soup? Columbia neuroscientists discovered a previously hidden full-body map inside the brain's secondary motor cortex (M2), found within its resting-state neural chatter, that orchestrates complex multi-limb actions.
category: Featured, Neuroscience, body map, brain research, coordination, movement, neurobiology, Zuckerman Institute

title: Irregular Sleep Schedules Tied to Depression & Loneliness
summary: When you sleep matters just as much as how long you sleep. Analyzing five months of smart-ring data from 23,000 adults, researchers found that irregular daily sleep-wake schedules weaken circadian alignment and correspond with severe depression, anxiety, and loneliness.
category: Featured, Neuroscience, Psychology, anxiety, brain research, circadian rhythm, depression, loneliness, mental health, neurobiology, Sleep, sleep-wake cycle, UCSF

title: 3D Genome Atlas Reveals Early Roots of Schizophrenia
summary: How does the human brain wire its reward and motor centers before birth? Using 3D genome sequencing across nearly 287,000 brain cells, UCLA scientists mapped the developing basal ganglia from mid-pregnancy to infancy, pinpointing how spiny projection neurons carry early genetic risk for schizophrenia.
category: Featured, Neuroscience, Psychology, brain development, brain mapping, brain research, developmental neuroscience, mental health, neurobiology, neurodevelopment, Schizophrenia, UCLA

title: Autism Shapes How Words vs. Numbers Drive Risk Decisions
summary: Words vs. numbers: A University of Tokyo study reveals that adults with autism spectrum disorder are strongly influenced by positive or negative verbal framing—such as "possible" versus "unlikely"—rather than underlying percentages when making medical decisions.
category: Autism, Featured, Neuroscience, ASD, brain research, decision making, language, neurobiology, numbers, Psychology, risk taking, University of Tokyo

title: Blood-Brain Barrier Protein Atlas Unlocks Alzheimer’s
summary: Does Alzheimer's start outside the brain? Gladstone Institutes researchers mapped the first atlas of 92 blood proteins that cross the blood-brain barrier, discovering that the barrier shuts down the import of protective liver proteins before it ever begins leaking toxins.
category: Featured, Neurology, Neuroscience, Alzheimer's disease, ApoA1, astrocytes, blood-brain barrier, brain research, cell, Genetics, Gladstone Institutes, liver-brain axis, neurobiology, neurodegeneration, Proteomics

title: Brain Moves Its Touch Center to Keep Feeling Sensation
summary: Why does artificial touch fade over time? Penn State engineers used fNIRS brain imaging to solve sensory habituation during transcutaneous nerve stimulation, discovering a 5-second pulse protocol that maintains a stable sense of touch while the brain recruits distributed networks.
category: Featured, Neuroscience, brain research, neurobiology, neuroprosthetics, Neurotech, Penn State, prosthetics, sensation, tactile perception, touch perception

title: Why Nervous System Hyperarousal Keeps Jolting You Awake
summary: Ever jolt awake with a racing heart just as you drift off? A study in PLOS Mental Health reveals that frequent hypnic jerks—or sleep starts—are not simple muscle twitches, but markers of anxiety, insomnia severity, and nervous system hyperarousal.
category: Featured, Neuroscience, anxiety, brain research, Hypnic Jerks, insomnia, mental health, neurobiology, PLOS, Psychology, Sleep, sleep disorders

title: Multiple Sclerosis Atrophy Spreads From High-Stress Neural Hubs
summary: Why does brain volume loss in multiple sclerosis follow distinct patterns? An MRI study of 2,187 patients reveals that atrophy originates in metabolically exhausted network hubs—including the thalamus and sensorimotor cortices—spreading outward along structural connections.
category: Featured, Neurology, Neuroscience, AAAS, brain research, Multiple Sclerosis, neurobiology
